'''Robert (Roy) Charles Geary''' (April 11, 1896 – February 8, 1983)<ref name=mathshis>{{Cite web |title=Robert Geary - Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Geary/ |access-date=2024-01-01 |website=Maths History |language=en}}</ref> was an Irish mathematician, [[statistician]] and founder of both the [[Central Statistics Office (Ireland)|Central Statistics Office]] and the [[Economic and Social Research Institute]]. Geary is known for his contributions to the estimation of [[errors-in-variables models]],<ref>{{cite book |last=Qin |first=Duo |title=The Formation of Econometrics: A Historical Perspective |location=New York |publisher=Oxford University Press |year=1993 |isbn=0-19-828388-1 |pages=86–87 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NIqMd5EX-CgC&pg=PA86 }}</ref> [[Geary's C]], the [[Geary–Khamis dollar]], the [[Stone–Geary utility function]], and Geary's theorem,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Geary |first=R. C. |date=1936 |title=The Distribution of "Student's" Ratio for Non-Normal Samples |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2983669 |journal=Supplement to the Journal of the Royal Statistical Society |volume=3 |issue=2 |pages=178–184 |doi=10.2307/2983669|jstor=2983669 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> which has that if the sample mean is distributed independently of the sample variance, then the population is [[normal distribution|distributed normally]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Laha |first=R. G. |date=1953 |title=On an extension of Geary's theorem |url=https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-lookup/doi/10.1093/biomet/40.1-2.228 |journal=Biometrika |language=en |volume=40 |issue=1–2 |pages=228–229 |doi=10.1093/biomet/40.1-2.228 |issn=0006-3444|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Citation |last=Spencer |first=J. E. |chapter=Robert Charles Geary |date=2001 |chapter-url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-1-4613-0179-0_98 |title=Statisticians of the Centuries |pages=459–463 |editor-last=Heyde |editor-first=C. C. |editor1-link=Chris Heyde|editor2-link=Eugene Seneta|access-date=2024-01-03 |place=New York, NY |publisher=Springer New York |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-1-4613-0179-0_98 |isbn=978-0-387-95283-3 |editor2-last=Seneta |editor2-first=E. |editor3-last=Crépel |editor3-first=P. |editor4-last=Fienberg |editor4-first=S. E.|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Spencer |first=J. E. |title=THE SCIENTIFIC WORK OF ROBERT CHARLES GEARY |url=http://www.tara.tcd.ie/bitstream/handle/2262/69062/v7n31976_1.pdf?sequence=1 |access-date=2024-01-03 |language=en}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Geary was born in [[Dublin|Dublin, Ireland]] and received his secondary education at the [[O'Connell School]]. He went on to study mathematics and mathematical physics at the [[University College Dublin]], where he obtained his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in 1916 and 1918, respectively. He was awarded a scholarship to continue his study at the [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]] in Paris, where he attended lectures by [[Émile Borel]], [[Élie Cartan]], [[Édouard Goursat]], [[Henri Lebesgue]], and [[Paul Langevin]]. Geary returned to Ireland in 1921, and was offered a lecturer position in mathematics at the [[University of Southampton]] (1922–23) and in applied economics at [[Cambridge University]] (1946–47).  He was a statistician in the Department of Industry and Commerce between 1923 and 1957. The [[National University of Ireland]] conferred a Doctorate of Science on him in 1938.<ref name=mathshis />

Geary was the founding director of the [[Central Statistics Office (Ireland)]] (in 1949). He was head of the [[National Accounts]] Branch of the [[United Nations]] in [[New York City|New York]] from 1957 to 1960. He was the founding director of the [[Economic and Social Research Institute]] (ESRI) in 1960 where he stayed till his retirement in 1966. He was an honorary fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] and the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]. In 1981, he won the [[Boyle Medal]].<ref>[https://www.rds.ie/Ireland-s-Philanthropic-Society/Our-Work/Projects/RDS-Irish-Times-Boyle-Medal-for-Scientific-Excelle/Boyle-Medal-Laureates Boyle Medal Laureates]  [[Royal Dublin Society]]</ref> To honour his contributions to social sciences, the UCD Geary Institute for Public Policy was named after him in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ucd.ie/geary/aboutus/|title=About Us &#124; UCD Geary Institute for Public Health}}</ref>
